title: Beyond Collision-Avoidance
subtitle: Physical Intelligence for Contact-Rich Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
overview: Contact can be a capability. This proposed workshop brings together aerial robotics, planning, control, learning and contact mechanics to explore how UAVs can interact with their surroundings, remain stable through impacts and recover when contact is unexpected.

themes.title: Plan with contact
themes.text: Coupled flight and end-effector planning, contact-inclusive motion planning and learned policies for inspection, perching and aerial manipulation.

themes.title: Regulate interaction
themes.text: Force and impedance control, contact sensing and estimation for stable, purposeful aerial interaction.

themes.title: Recover from impact
themes.text: Collision detection, state estimation and resilient control when contact is unintended.

themes.title: Learn across environments
themes.text: Reinforcement learning and sim-to-real transfer for changing surfaces, uncertain dynamics and contact transitions.

themes.title: Design for physical intelligence
themes.text: Compliance, morphology and reconfiguration that expand what aerial planning and control can achieve.

themes.title: Compare meaningful capabilities
themes.text: Shared tasks, metrics and evaluation practices for contact-aware UAVs and their real-world deployment.

contributions.description: We plan to invite 2–4-page extended abstracts in IEEE format, with up to 30 posters and six lightning talks reserved for PhD students, postdocs and faculty within three years of their first independent appointment, with career breaks considered. Each submission is planned to receive two reviews. Industry and academic contributions are welcome.
contributions.submission: The planned submission platform is OpenReview. A submission link and final instructions will be released after workshop acceptance.
contributions.datesNote: Tentative dates, subject to the conference schedule and workshop acceptance.
contributions.publication: Accepted contributions are intended for the workshop website, with author permission, and are separate from the IEEE proceedings. Any collective preprint or follow-up perspective will depend on author agreement and editorial feasibility.

participation.title: Bring an idea
participation.text: Share early results, open problems or a reproducible evaluation task. After acceptance, organizers plan to assign mentors for early-career contributors and offer feedback through poster discussions.

participation.title: Show the mechanism
participation.text: Authors may propose static displays and videos of contact-capable UAVs. Displays depend on space and organizer approval; no flight demonstrations are planned.

participation.title: Shape the discussion
participation.text: Audience questions will inform the moderated discussion and closing panel. We aim to identify shared challenges and useful evaluation practices.
